summary: Hans Krahe was a linguist who held posts at the University of Würzburg (~1936–1947), the University of Heidelberg (~1947–1949), and the University of Tübingen (~1949–1965).

Hans Küng worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the Pontifical Gregorian University and Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum (~1948–1955), and the Catholic University of Paris (~1955–1956), later holding a post at the University of Tübingen (~1960–1996).

Hans T. Bakker is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Jacob Ensink (~1972–1982). He held posts at the University of Groningen (~1986–2013), All Souls College, Oxford (~2008–2009), and the British Museum (2014).
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (~1926–1929), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1929–1935).

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp (~1959–1963) and Gustav Mensching (~1960–1964), whom he succeeded at the University of Bonn as Direktor in 1972.
Hans-Werbin Köhler is an Indologist who studied under Eduard Hermann and under doctoral supervisor Ernst Waldschmidt (attested 1973).
Hansa Dhammahaso is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who held director posts at the International Buddhist Studies College and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2017).
Hanung Kim specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. Kim earned a master's degree at Columbia University and a PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.
Har Dayal was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He pursued studies at the University of Delhi and at SOAS University of London (~1927–1930).
Har Dutt Sharma was an Indologist who served as Reader in Sanskrit at the University of Delhi and held a post at Hindu College, University of Delhi (attested 1957).

Hara Prasad Sastri worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and Joint Philological Secretary at The Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).
Harabhatta Sastri was an Indologist who held posts at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, including as a pandit (attested 1918, 1922, and 1945).
Harabhatha Shastri was an Indologist who held posts at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir, including serving as a Pandit (attested 1911 and 1916).

Harald Hauptmann was an archaeologist who studied at Tübingen, Saarland, Heidelberg (~1958–1964), and FU Berlin (until 1978). He held posts at the German Archaeological Institute (1966–1971; Istanbul 1994–2001) and Heidelberg University (1978; 1980–1994).
Harald Hundius was a scholar in linguistics and Buddhist studies who studied under Singkha Wannasai. In 1983, he held a post as lecturer at Chiang Mai University.

Haraprasad Shastri was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and historian. Educated at Presidency University and Sanskrit College, he held posts at Benares Sanskrit College (1883; 1900–1908), Presidency College (1895), and the University of Dhaka (1921–1924).

Hari Damodar Velankar was an Indologist who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944–1948) and Joint Director at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).
Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Ramakant Tripathi and Jan Willem de Jong.

Haridas Bhattacharyya worked in philosophy and religious studies, studying at Scottish Church College (~1908–1912) and the University of Calcutta (~1912–1914). He held posts at Scottish Church College (1915), Calcutta (1917), Dhaka (1921), and Banaras Hindu University (1947).
Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi is an Indologist who studied under Karunapati Tripathi and served as Publication Officer at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1996).
